quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Rely only on your mirrors to see all around you.
Point in the direction you plan to turn.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Mirrors alone are not enough.

questions.question: A car is entering the highway from a ramp on your right. The driver may not see your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left side of your lane so they can share it if needed.
Move into another lane, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane, if necessary.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of space to vehicles entering the highway from a ramp. Move to another lane away from the ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give them room to enter safely.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you assume?

options.text: Other drivers can see your motorcycle as easily as other vehicles.
You do not need to worry about whether other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer and smaller lights than other vehicles. They are hard to see. Ride defensively and assume other drivers do not see you.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what is true?

options.text: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You can complete the pass in a no passing zone if you started before the zone began.
You can exceed the speed limit.
You should pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must follow the posted speed limit and only happen in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: A vehicle is following you too closely. What should you do?

options.text: Allow the other driver to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the other driver to pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. Change lanes safely and let them get ahead. Speeding up will only make things more dangerous.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, what happens?

options.text: The motorcycle could lurch and the rear tire could skid.
The motorcycle could accelerate too quickly.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle could lurch and the rear tire could skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle will lurch and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: Your motorcycle starts to weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Grip the handlebars tighter and speed up to get past the hazard.
Ride on the shoulder instead of on the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is normal and not dangerous. Relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: If your motorcycle has a load in the sidecar, the stopping distance:

options.text: Will be the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: May increase.
questions.explanation: Adding weight to a motorcycle increases its stopping distance. Start braking and slowing down earlier when your motorcycle has a load or passenger in a sidecar.

questions.question: How can you help drivers merging onto the highway from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Move into another lane, if possible.
Do not worry about it since they are merging.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane, if possible.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging onto the highway may not see your motorcycle. Give them space by moving into a different lane if you can.

questions.question: What is a major effect of drinking alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slower body functions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows down your body and mind. It makes both physical and mental functions weaker.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Close the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop as fast as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly. Slow down by easing off the throttle and keeping a straight path. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake on the tire that is still good. Move toward the side of the road as you slow down, then stop.

questions.question: Which of these protects a rider best?

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. Wear boots or shoes that are tall and sturdy to cover your ankles. Use low heels so they don't catch on foot pegs. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and improve your grip on the controls.

questions.question: When you adjust your mirrors, what should you see?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the lane next to you as possible. A mirror may show part of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors?
questions.correctAnswerText: Often
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to watch for hazards behind you.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, how does stopping compare to riding without a sidecar?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping takes longer.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight, which requires more braking force. Stopping takes longer going downhill than on flat ground.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Go faster to get off the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: Close the throttle and keep the motorcycle straight as you slow down. If you need to brake, slowly apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: Which is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain
Limit how far you ride in one day

questions.correctAnswerText: Take artificial stimulants
questions.explanation: Take breaks often and do not ride more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from the weather. Do not use artificial stimulants because when they wear off, the danger can be very serious.

questions.question: Which item does NOT help protect you from serious injury?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ear buds
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and pants, tall boots to cover your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks, what should you do?

options.text: Keep holding the brake and the skid will stop.
Release the front brake and do not use it again.
Release the front brake and then squeeze it quickly.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the front brake completely right away. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: The body removes about one alcoholic drink per hour. Someone had eight drinks four hours ago. How many drinks are probably still in their body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four drinks
questions.explanation: To estimate drinks remaining in the body, subtract the number of hours from the total drinks consumed. In this case, eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining.

questions.question: What should a passenger do while riding?

options.text: Lean the same way the rider leans.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the same way the rider leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should lean with the rider during turns and curves. They should hold onto the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do to avoid injury on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Go slower.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down. Sudden movements can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid the slippery road.

questions.question: Why is riding beside another vehicle dangerous?

options.text: You may have trouble reaching a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It stops other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding beside another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The driver may not see you and could move into your lane. The vehicle also blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.
